description: Six cohesive 8-bit rubber-hose clown designs generated by PixelLab on 2026-10-02 and retargeted to the established twelve-frame riding and juggling rig.
why: Owner requested a consistent 8-bit rubber-hose redesign of the tent, title and all six clowns, retaining fixed five-tone day/night colors without animation palette flicker.
style: 1930s-50s rubber-hose animation (the owner's reference: MOUSE: P.I. For Hire; Fleischer's Koko the Clown): jointless bendy limbs, oversized white gloves, pie-cut eyes, big shoes, a one-pixel near-black outline, in the owner's navy and white carried by a five-tone navy ramp (the old cartoons' greys), shaded like classic pixel-art sprites with the light from the upper left and the far leg a tone darker than the near one; motion on the circus beat (0.3 s: three 0.1 s ride frames).

palette.description: The riders' indexed five-tone palette (2026-09-28). The packaged strips store each pixel as its day colour; the app redraws the same indices in the ramp of the surface it sits on.

roles.1: outline and deepest: line art, the tyre
roles.2: dark fill: suits, hats, dark shoe parts, the far leg, the saddle and post, the far crank
roles.3: mid: shading, the near leg's shading, spokes, the tyre's highlight arc
roles.4: light: shading on white areas, highlights on dark, the hub, the near crank
roles.5: white: face, gloves, collar, shoe highlights

night.surface: Home in dark appearance and the empty-chat landings on slate #27313F

palette.checks: ClownToneTests: both ramps run dark to light with neighbouring tones at least 1.5:1 and 15 L* apart; the day outline is 16.0:1 on paper, the day fill 9.2:1 and the mid tone 4.3:1; the night outline stays darker than slate and the night fill is 2.63:1 on slate (2.86:1 on Increase Contrast's #222B38), white 13.2:1.

steps.design: Reviewed native96px PixelLab Pro Flash source stills from branding/candidates/rubber-hose-20261002/manifest.json.
steps.reference: PixelLab Pro Flash removed unicycle props for five riders. The patched-coat rider uses PixelLab guarded deletion of235 wheel/post pixels. References retain native96px detail, with manually measured initial joints.
steps.skeleton: Existing source/pose.py places reference hips on saddle on a128px transparent canvas with16px margins, writes12 frames of pedal/hand target poses.
steps.ride: PixelLab animate_with_skeleton_v3,12 frames per design, south-east, side view, mannequin, rhythmic arm and leg motion; no drawn limbs.
steps.palette: PixelLab reduce_colors processes all12 frames together with the same explicit five day tones, no dithering. Exact subsequent repairs preserve this palette.
steps.exactRepairs: PixelLab guarded glove-pixel translations for dropped inward gloves in whiteface/tramp/harlequin/ringmaster/strongman frames02/08. Patched-coat frame11 uses intact same-hand-phase frame05 pixels, followed by exact deletion of an11px disconnected remnant.
steps.legToneSeparation: Existing tone2→3 near, tone3→2 far; posed leg paths within4px below saddle to lower ankle; near owns overlaps. Outlines/light highlights untouched. Exact PixelLab guarded patches are reproducibly planned by candidates/rubber-hose-20261002/rigged/leg-tones.py; all six updated workbench IDs are recorded.
steps.motionPolish: PixelLab exact guarded edits preserve canonical head/hat/chest materials through the bob and repeat six arm poses. Static source trouser pixels are protected from moving-bone recoloring. Each design reuses its own shoe pixels at a constant sole anchor on each pedal, with one fixed darker far-shoe ramp and explicit shoe ownership. Recipes and immutable outputs: candidates/clown-motion-polish-20261002/.

rig.unicycle: hub (45, 82), crank 5 px, wheel radius 12 (ground row 94), saddle top at (45, 62)
rig.legs: Both hips on the saddle, 4 px apart for the three-quarter view: right (43, 59.5), left (47, 58.5). The feet stay on the crank circle 180 degrees apart through one clockwise turn in 12 frames (frame 0: the near foot at the bottom). Each ankle sits 7 px above and 2 px behind its pedal, where the big shoe's sole meets the pedal. Knees are solved from an 11 px thigh and a 14 px shin and always bend forward, so the legs alternate, one reaching down while the other folds, never both bent together.
rig.bob: The head, neck and shoulders drop 1 px on every beat (frames 0, 3, 6 and 9); the hips stay on the saddle.
rig.hands: A cascade hand path (throw inside, catch outside, scoop along the bottom), six frames a cycle, the hands half a cycle apart, around points 10-11 px either side of the neck and 11 px below the shoulders.
rig.cranks: rig.json records each frame's crank angle; the packaging draws the cranks and pedals at exactly that angle, under the posed feet.
rig.depth: Pixels nearest the posed far leg go behind the unicycle. Explicit shoe-ownership.json and leg-ownership.json override that heuristic; near thigh/shoe and protected foreground remain above the saddle and wheel. Validated ownership sets are opaque, inside the crop and mutually disjoint.

packaging.tones: Each 128px export is cropped to its centre96px and mapped to the five day tones. The packager rejects excessive stray colors, broken silhouettes and frames with fewer than four tones. Current source frames use the exact five-tone ramp. Specks of one or two pixels are removed before composition.
packaging.unicycle: Drawn in tones, back to front: the far crank and pedal (2), the tyre, a 2 px ring of radius 12 (1) with a highlight on its outer row at the upper left (3), four spokes turning with the cranks (3; four, since a 30-degree step on eight spokes would seem to turn backwards), the post and saddle (2), the 3 px hub (4), the near crank and pedal (4); the rider's far leg behind all of it (rig.depth).
packaging.sheet: ClownRide-<design>.png: twelve 96 px frames, each pixel transparent or exactly its day tone; ClownRide-<design>.json: the rig (frame duration, beat, ground, measured palms, crank angles) and both ramps. The app maps each pixel back to its index and draws the day ramp on a light backdrop (Home on paper) and the night ramp on a dark one (Home in dark appearance, the empty-chat landings on slate), picked from the backdrop the scene resolves; a two-pixel ring outside the silhouette is drawn in the backdrop where the rider crosses the tent.
packaging.checks: Stops without writing if a palm falls back to its posed target, ownership is invalid, the rider reaches the ground row or a frame fails visual checks. Palm centroids use tone-4/5 pixels within 6 px of the wrist, restricted to explicit foreground when present to exclude costume highlights. All six designs: 24 of 24 palms, the wheel alone on row 93.
packaging.limits: Large rubber-hose shoes overlap the hub and crank in the lower half of the turn. At least70% of the tyre remains visible in every frame; the full hub and spokes show in the upper half. At the top of the turn, the visible near crank stem ends beneath the shoe on the pedal, with source-shoe occlusion verified explicitly.
packaging.cleanup: Fixed day palette already applied jointly by PixelLab; packaging verifies all frames and crops their128px canvases to96px. Only exported one/two-pixel specks are omitted. The existing unicycle/far-leg composition supplies stable tire, saddle, crank and spokes.
packaging.palette: Exact existing five indexed day/night tones; one explicit shared palette across all frames, no learned per-frame palette.
packaging.verification: All 72 frames pass exact palette, silhouette, ground, protected glove-contact and owned thigh-fill checks. Branding suite: 94 tests, 8 optional export skips, 0 failures; includes original raised-knee coverage, near-thigh saddle overlap, costume colors, shoe shape, source leg contrast and wheel/crank visibility.

juggling.loop: 168 beats of 0.3 s (50.4 s) = eight 6.3 s trips around the tent = 42 ride loops; the loop is seamless
juggling.phrases: three-ball cascade, then four (beats 48-65) and five (beats 66-89), then three again; extra balls come out of a pocket or are put away
juggling.drops: missed catches landing on beats 88 and 131; the ball bounces (restitution 0.6) and rolls away from wherever the clown is, a new ball comes out 14 beats later
juggling.window: a performance shows only balls taken out after it joins the ring and throws none after it stops, so each clown starts with empty hands and finishes its catches before riding back in

choreography.reveal: at the reveal (the next 0.3 s beat) a clown fades in inside the doorway, centre (121.5, 250.5), wheel on the threshold (y 285), in three 0.1 s steps; it is drawn between the doorway's fill and the tent, masked by TentDoorway.png, and in front of the tent below the threshold
choreography.out: it rides 54 units straight out in 0.456 s (about the orbit's pace) to the orbit's pass by the door, angle 112 degrees, centre (123.1, 304.6), then circles every 6.3 s and juggles
choreography.back: after a seeded 40-90 s it throws no more; at the first pass by the door at least a beat after its last catch it rides back in (0.456 s) and fades out in three steps
choreography.next: the doorway stays empty a seeded 4-10 s, then the next design comes out: shuffled, never the same twice in a row
choreography.clock: the ride frames run on the circus clock; each performance juggles on its own clock, whole 1.2 s ride loops from it, placed so the orbit and the juggling line up as on the circus clock's reference lap (the title's clearance is measured there)
choreography.seed: the reveal moment (milliseconds since the reference date), so a reveal always gives the same performance
choreography.cover: the opening cover shows no clown
